title: Choose the visual world for Libertas Forum
question: The roll assigned Passbook & Clearing. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Passbook & Clearing
options.lineage: Indian bank passbooks and cheque clearing: posting stamps, return memos, pencilled clerk notes
options.thesis: Every alert posts like an uncleared cheque; the deep lane then clears it or returns it with a reason.
options.viewport: Navy cover rail; a posting queue of alerts ranked by urgency whose status stamps turn UNCLEARED to CLEARED or RETURNED live; the selected entry's voucher beside it.
options.risk: Overplay the banking grammar and it reads as a bank app; it must live in states, ink and figures only.

raised.raise: Clearing restyles an entry in place: rows keep identity and position when the deep lane rules, nothing jumps.
Every voucher ends in a Next actions strip offering only what is possible now: build pack, notify, assign.
No decorative chrome: hierarchy comes from figures and type weight, never card shadows.
Every entity carries a short citable code (ALT-0037, ACT-02, CLU-6688) so officers can say it aloud.

options.label: Message Precedence
options.lineage: Police wireless message pads: precedence (FLASH, IMMEDIATE, PRIORITY, ROUTINE) and date-time groups
options.thesis: Every alert is a signal message with a precedence and a date-time group, logged until acknowledged.
options.viewport: Khaki-olive rail; a message log sorted by precedence and DTG; the open message as a signal form with action-taken lines.
options.risk: Topped my list, but it is the familiar route: precedence codes behave like any SOC severity column.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: boarding passes and live airport gate boards
options.thesis: Alerts rerank in place and a changed verdict stays lit until an officer acknowledges it.
options.viewport: A ranked board of alerts with a pass-style stub for the selected one; changes flash and hold.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds product clarity (persistent change state); loses audience identification for police officers.
options.risk: Reads as travel software if the stubs dominate.

options.label: Course Over Terrain
options.lineage: orienteering maps: fixed terrain colours, one purple course line
options.thesis: Context stays a muted fixed language; the active evidence path rides above it in one reserved colour.
options.viewport: The relationship graph as terrain with the evidence path drawn as the course, control by control.
options.case: Holds product clarity for the graph and evidence paths; loses audience identification and says little about the alert queue.
options.risk: Strong for one view, thin as a whole console.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Live rows ranked by time with per-character flips.
options.viewport: A black departures board of alerts.
options.case: Spectacle over evidence: reads as the flashy look you ruled out, and time-ranking fights urgency.
options.kept: A state change restyles the row in place without breaking the grid.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Each junction shows only the choices ahead.
options.viewport: Yellow bands naming the next decision.
options.case: Loud and foreign to a police console.
options.kept: Show only the next possible actions at each decision point.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Chrome deleted; type is the interface.
options.case: Toy-like and generic, both on your avoid list.
options.kept: Hierarchy from type and figures, not decoration.

options.label: Coded Catalog Grid
options.lineage: printed event catalogs with table codes
options.thesis: Every cell has a code that maps to a place.
options.case: Pop-culture register, unprofessional for this audience.
options.kept: Short citable codes for every entity.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A threat-intelligence console as SOC vendors ship it, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Left nav, KPI cards on top, an alert table and charts below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any SOC product the judges have already seen.
